title: The 231 MPH Gust Measured on Mount Washington
asof: Figures from Mount Washington Observatory & FOX Weather · full video on the channel

shots.s: April 1934. Three men on a mountaintop measure something nobody had ever seen.
The Mount Washington Observatory, in New Hampshire.
Sal Pagliuca, Alex McKenzie and Wendell Stephenson were on duty.
Their anemometer had a heater built in, so ice couldn't jam it.
Then a gust hit two hundred thirty-one miles an hour.
For decades, it was the fastest wind ever measured on Earth's surface.
CBS reported it's still the fastest recorded by a person on land.
And in 2023, the wind chill up here hit minus one hundred eight Fahrenheit.
Would you stand on that deck?
